findings.issue: No ErrorBoundary anywhere; a non-404 failure of the upstream API throws out of createAsync during SSR or client navigation and takes down the whole page with no recovery UI.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the route outlet in solid-js's ErrorBoundary inside the Router root (with a fallback and a link home).

findings.issue: A pending search-debounce timer fires after a pagination link was clicked and does setParams({q, page: undefined}, {replace:true}), stripping the page the user just navigated to.
findings.suggestion: Cancel the debounce on any navigation (e.g. in the pagination onClick or via an on cleanup tied to page()), or only set `q` in the deferred setParams.

findings.issue: The typesById construction is a near-duplicate of the one in homeList (lines 152-170); a change to how card types are derived must be made twice.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared `typesByPokemonId()` helper (built from allTypes()) used by both homeList and teamDetails.

findings.issue: The sprite URL template is built inline in three places (114, 185, 341).
A single ~440-line module owns the fetch cache, the API client and all domain shaping for every page; it will become the merge hotspot as pages grow.
findings.suggestion: Split the cache/fetch client (api, mapLimit, listAll) from the per-resource shaping functions; the queries.ts facade already gives the right seam.

findings.issue: First-value-of-search-param logic is re-implemented inline here while index.tsx:6 has a `first()` helper.
findings.suggestion: Move `first()` into lib/format (or a small router-utils module) and reuse it.

findings.issue: getTeamDetails([]) is called (a server round-trip plus a full types fetch) even when the team is empty and the result is never shown.
findings.suggestion: Guard the createAsync fetcher: `team.team().length ? getTeamDetails(team.team()) : null`.

findings.issue: No typecheck/lint script and no devDependencies section; CI has nothing to run and types are only checked incidentally.
findings.suggestion: Add `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"` (and a lint script) and wire them into the harness's test command.

summary: This is a genuinely idiomatic SolidStart v2 codebase — query/"use server" data loading, route preloads, URL-held filter state, a cookie-backed context store for the team feature, and 404s surfaced as both UI and status — that I'd merge after one review round. The weaknesses are all local and cheap to fix: a missing ErrorBoundary, a 150 ms debounce/pagination race, and three small DRY violations inside the one large server data module.
